nodes.summary: Let $n \ge 1$ and let $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ be a full-dimensional convex body with Lebesgue measure $\mathrm{Vol}(K)$ and uniform density $f_K$, equal to $1/\mathrm{Vol}(K)$ on $K$ and to $0$ outside $K$. Then the differential entropy $-\int_{\mathbb{R}^n} f_K(x) \log f_K(x) \, dx$ of $f_K$ equals $\log \mathrm{Vol}(K)$.
nodes.title: Entropy of the uniform density of a convex body

nodes.summary: Let $n \ge 1$ and let $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ be a full-dimensional convex body, so that its Lebesgue measure $\mathrm{Vol}(K)$ is finite and positive. The uniform density of $K$ is the function $f_K \colon \mathbb{R}^n \to \mathbb{R}$ equal to $1/\mathrm{Vol}(K)$ on $K$ and to $0$ outside $K$.
nodes.title: Uniform density of a convex body

nodes.summary: For a full-dimensional convex body $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$, this is the intrinsic log-concave law on $\mathbb{R}^n$ of intrinsic dimension $n$ whose chart is the identity map of $\mathbb{R}^n$, whose law is the uniform probability law on $K$, and whose coordinate law is that uniform law viewed as a log-concave law with density $\mathbf{1}_K / \operatorname{vol}(K)$.
nodes.title: The uniform law on a convex body as an intrinsic log-concave law

nodes.summary: For a full-dimensional convex body $K$ in $\mathbb{R}^n$, let $\operatorname{Cov}(K)$ be the covariance matrix of the uniform probability law on $K$ and let $\operatorname{vol}(K)$ be the Lebesgue volume of $K$. The isotropic constant of $K$ is the real number $L_K = \left(\det \operatorname{Cov}(K) / \operatorname{vol}(K)^2\right)^{1/(2n)}$.
nodes.title: Isotropic constant of a convex body

nodes.summary: For a full-dimensional convex body $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ (a convex body with nonempty interior, $n > 0$), the affine span of the support of the uniform probability law on $K$ is all of $\mathbb{R}^n$.
nodes.title: The uniform law on a convex body spans the whole space

nodes.summary: For a full-dimensional convex body $K$ in $\mathbb{R}^n$, the uniform law on $K$ is the probability measure obtained by restricting Lebesgue measure to $K$ and dividing by the volume of $K$; it gives a set $A$ the mass $\operatorname{vol}(A \cap K) / \operatorname{vol}(K)$.
nodes.title: Uniform distribution on a convex body

nodes.summary: Let $n \ge 1$ and let $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ be a full-dimensional convex body of Lebesgue measure $\mathrm{Vol}(K)$, with uniform probability measure $\lambda_K$, uniform density $f_K$, and covariance matrix $C_K$ of the coordinates under $\lambda_K$. Then the entropy isotropic constant of the uniform law of $K$ equals the isotropic constant of $K$, that is,…
nodes.title: The entropy and volume isotropic constants of a convex body agree

nodes.summary: Let $n \ge 1$ and let $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ be a full-dimensional convex body of Lebesgue measure $\mathrm{Vol}(K)$. The uniform law of $K$ is the log-concave law on $\mathbb{R}^n$ whose probability measure is Lebesgue measure restricted to $K$ and divided by $\mathrm{Vol}(K)$, and whose density is the uniform density of $K$.
nodes.title: Uniform law of a convex body

nodes.summary: This is the value $\sup_{n \ge 1} \sup_K L_K \in [0, \infty]$, where for each dimension $n \ge 1$ the inner supremum runs over all full-dimensional convex bodies $K$ in $\mathbb{R}^n$ and $L_K$ is the isotropic constant of $K$.
nodes.title: Supremum of isotropic constants of convex bodies

nodes.summary: This is the value $\sup_{n \ge 1} \sup_K L_K \in [0, \infty]$, where for each dimension $n \ge 1$ the inner supremum runs over the full-dimensional convex bodies $K$ in $\mathbb{R}^n$ that are centrally symmetric, that is $K = -K$, and $L_K$ is the isotropic constant of $K$.
nodes.title: Supremum of isotropic constants of symmetric convex bodies

nodes.summary: Let $\mu$ be a measure on a measurable space $\alpha$ and let $K \subseteq \alpha$ be a measurable set with $\mu(K) \neq 0$. Then the conditional measure $\mu(\cdot \mid K)$, that is $\mu(K)^{-1}$ times the restriction of $\mu$ to $K$, equals the measure with density $x \mapsto \mu(K)^{-1} \mathbf{1}_K(x)$ with respect to $\mu$. Here $\mu(K)^{-1}$ is taken in $[0, \infty]$, so it is $0$ when $\mu(K) = \infty$.
nodes.title: Conditioning on a set is the normalized indicator density

nodes.summary: If $\mu$ is an isotropic log-concave probability measure on $\mathbb{R}^n$, then the covariance matrix of $\mu$ is the $n \times n$ identity matrix.
nodes.title: Isotropic log-concave laws have identity covariance

nodes.summary: For every log-concave law $\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$, the covariance matrix of $\mu$ is positive semidefinite.
nodes.title: Covariance matrices of log-concave laws are positive semidefinite

nodes.summary: For a measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$, the covariance matrix of $\mu$ is the $n \times n$ real matrix whose $(i, j)$ entry is $\int (x_i - m_i)(x_j - m_j) \, d\mu(x)$, where $m_i = \int x_i \, d\mu(x)$ is the mean of the $i$-th coordinate.
nodes.title: Covariance matrix

nodes.summary: For a function $f \colon \mathbb{R}^n \to \mathbb{R}$, usually the Lebesgue density of a probability law, the differential entropy of $f$ is $-\int_{\mathbb{R}^n} f(x) \log f(x) \, dx$, with the natural logarithm and $0 \log 0 = 0$.
nodes.title: Differential entropy

nodes.summary: For every $n \in \mathbb{N}$, the supremum of the isotropic constants of full-dimensional convex bodies in $\mathbb{R}^n$ is at most the supremum of the entropy isotropic constants of probability laws on $\mathbb{R}^n$ with a log-concave Lebesgue density $f$ such that every coordinate $x_i$ and every product $x_i x_j$ is integrable under the law and $f \log f$ is Lebesgue integrable, both suprema taken in…
nodes.title: Body isotropic constants are bounded by the law supremum

nodes.summary: For $n \in \mathbb{N}$, this is $\sup_K L_K \in [0, \infty]$, the supremum of the isotropic constants $L_K$ over all full-dimensional convex bodies $K$ in $\mathbb{R}^n$. Full-dimensional convex bodies are taken only in dimension $n \ge 1$, so for $n = 0$ the supremum is over the empty family and is $0$.
nodes.title: Supremum of isotropic constants in a fixed dimension

nodes.summary: For a natural number $N$, this is the supremum in $[0, \infty]$ of the isotropic constants $L_\mu$ over all intrinsic log-concave laws $\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}^N$.
nodes.title: Supremum of intrinsic isotropic constants in a fixed ambient dimension

nodes.summary: For $n \in \mathbb{N}$, this is $\sup_\mu L_\mu \in [0, \infty]$, the supremum of the isotropic constants $L_\mu = e^{-\operatorname{Ent}(f)/n} (\det \operatorname{Cov}(\mu))^{1/(2n)}$ over all log-concave laws $\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$, where $f$ is the log-concave Lebesgue density of $\mu$, $\operatorname{Ent}(f)$ its differential entropy and $\operatorname{Cov}(\mu)$ its covariance matrix. Here a log-concave law…
nodes.title: Supremum of entropic isotropic constants in a fixed dimension

nodes.summary:
The entropy isotropic constant, the supremum of the isotropic constants of intrinsic log-concave laws over all ambient dimensions $N > 0$, is at most the supremum in $[0, \infty]$, over all dimensions $n > 0$ and all log-concave laws $
u$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$, of the entropy isotropic constant $L_
u = e^{-h(f)/n} \det(\operatorname{Cov} 
u)^{1/(2n)}$, where $f$ is the density of $
u$ and $h(f) = -\int f \log f$.
nodes.title: The entropy isotropic constant is at most the full-dimensional supremum

nodes.summary: This is the supremum, in $[0, \infty]$, over all dimensions $N > 0$ of the supremum of the isotropic constants $L_\mu$ over all intrinsic log-concave laws $\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}^N$. A law supported on a proper affine subspace thus contributes the isotropic constant computed in orthonormal coordinates on its affine span.
nodes.title: Entropy-convention isotropic constant

nodes.summary: For a natural number $n$, a full-dimensional convex body in dimension $n$ is a nonempty compact convex set $K$ in the Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^n$ whose interior is nonempty, where $n$ is required to be positive.
nodes.title: Full-dimensional convex body

nodes.summary: This is the supremum, in $[0, \infty]$, of the isotropic constant $L_\mu = e^{-h(f)/n} (\det \mathrm{Cov}(\mu))^{1/(2n)}$ over all positive integers $n$ and all log-concave laws $\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$ with Lebesgue density $f$, where $h(f) = -\int_{\mathbb{R}^n} f \log f$ is the differential entropy of $f$ and $\mathrm{Cov}(\mu)$ is the covariance matrix of the coordinates under $\mu$.
nodes.title: Supremum of the isotropic constant over full-dimensional log-concave laws

nodes.summary: For a real number $a > 0$, this is the closed interval $[-a, a]$ in the one-dimensional Euclidean space, regarded as a full-dimensional convex body.
nodes.title: Symmetric interval as a convex body

nodes.summary: Let $\mu$ be an intrinsic log-concave law on $\mathbb{R}^N$, given by a log-concave law $\nu$ on $\mathbb{R}^d$ with density $f$ and an affine isometric embedding of $\mathbb{R}^d$ onto the affine span of the support of $\mu$. The isotropic constant of $\mu$ is the entropy isotropic constant of $\nu$,
nodes.title: Isotropic constant of an intrinsic log-concave law

nodes.summary: Fix an ambient dimension $N$. An intrinsic log-concave law on $\mathbb{R}^N$ consists of a dimension $d$, a log-concave law $\nu$ on $\mathbb{R}^d$ (that is, $d > 0$ and $\nu$ is a probability measure with a log-concave Lebesgue density $f$, integrable coordinates and coordinate products, and integrable $f \log f$), an affine isometric embedding $\varphi : \mathbb{R}^d \to \mathbb{R}^N$ of Euclidean spaces, and a…
nodes.title: Log-concave law in intrinsic coordinates

nodes.summary: The supremum, over all positive integers $n$ and all full-dimensional convex bodies $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$, of the isotropic constant $L_K = \left(\det \mathrm{Cov}(K) / \mathrm{Vol}(K)^2\right)^{1/(2n)}$, where $\mathrm{Cov}(K)$ is the covariance matrix of the uniform distribution on $K$, is at least $1/\sqrt{12}$.
nodes.title: Cube lower bound for the supremal isotropic constant

nodes.summary: For a natural number $n$, a full-dimensional convex body $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ is centrally symmetric when $K = -K$, that is, for every $x \in \mathbb{R}^n$, $x \in K$ if and only if $-x \in K$.
nodes.title: Centrally symmetric convex body

nodes.summary: Let $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ be a measurable convex set and let $c > 0$. Then the function equal to $c$ on $K$ and to $0$ outside $K$ is a log-concave density.
nodes.title: Constant densities on convex sets are log-concave

nodes.summary: For a log-concave law $\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$ with Lebesgue density $f$, the isotropic constant of $\mu$ is $L_\mu = e^{-h(f)/n} (\det \mathrm{Cov}(\mu))^{1/(2n)}$, where $h(f) = -\int_{\mathbb{R}^n} f \log f$ is the differential entropy of $f$ and $\mathrm{Cov}(\mu)$ is the covariance matrix of the coordinates under $\mu$.
nodes.title: Isotropic constant of a log-concave law

nodes.summary: The linear isometric isomorphism from $\mathbb{R}$ onto one-dimensional Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^1$ that sends a real number $x$ to the vector whose only coordinate is $x$.
nodes.title: Identification of the line with one-dimensional Euclidean space

nodes.summary: For a positive integer $n$, a log-concave law on $\mathbb{R}^n$ is a probability measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$ together with a Lebesgue density $f$ of $\mu$ that is log-concave: $f$ is measurable and nonnegative, and $f((1-t)x + ty) \ge f(x)^{1-t} f(y)^t$ for all $x, y \in \mathbb{R}^n$ and $0 < t < 1$. Moreover every coordinate $x_i$ and every product $x_i x_j$ is $\mu$-integrable, and $f \log f$ is Lebesgue…
nodes.title: Log-concave law

nodes.summary: For a natural number $n$, the squared-radius thin-shell width in dimension $n$ is the supremum, in $[0, \infty]$, of $\left(\int (|x|^2 - n)^2 \, d\mu(x) / n\right)^{1/2}$ (with $0/0 = 0$) over all isotropic log-concave probability measures $\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$, that is, those with a log-concave Lebesgue density, mean zero and identity covariance.
nodes.title: Squared-radius thin-shell width

nodes.summary: For a real number $a$, the set of points of one-dimensional Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^1$ whose only coordinate lies in the closed interval $[-a, a]$. It is empty when $a < 0$.
nodes.title: Symmetric interval in one-dimensional Euclidean space

nodes.summary: The uniform distribution on the symmetric interval $[-1, 1]$ of one-dimensional Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^1$ is not an isotropic log-concave probability measure.
nodes.title: The uniform law on (−1, 1) is not isotropic log-concave

nodes.summary: Let $\mu$ be the uniform distribution on the symmetric interval $[-\sqrt{3}, \sqrt{3}]$ of one-dimensional Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^1$. Then $\int (\|x\| - \sqrt{1})^2 \, d\mu(x)$, the mean squared deviation of the Euclidean norm from $\sqrt{1} = 1$, is at most the thin-shell variance constant.
nodes.title: Radius fluctuation of the uniform law on (−√3, √3)

nodes.summary: The uniform distribution on the symmetric interval $[-\sqrt{3}, \sqrt{3}]$ of one-dimensional Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^1$ is an isotropic log-concave probability measure: it has a log-concave density with respect to Lebesgue measure, mean zero and identity covariance.
nodes.title: The uniform law on (−√3, √3) is isotropic log-concave

nodes.summary: Let $\mu$ be the uniform distribution on the symmetric interval $[-\sqrt{3}, \sqrt{3}]$ of one-dimensional Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^1$. Its normalized radius variance $\int (\|x\|^2 - 1)^2 \, d\mu(x)$ is at most the thin-shell variance constant, the supremum of the normalized radius variance over all isotropic log-concave probability measures in all positive dimensions.
nodes.title: Thin-shell variance bound for the uniform law on (−√3, √3)

nodes.summary: For a real number $a$, the measure on one-dimensional Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^1$ obtained by conditioning Lebesgue measure on the set $\{x : -a \le x_1 \le a\}$ of points whose only coordinate $x_1$ lies in $[-a, a]$, that is, Lebesgue measure restricted to this set and divided by its measure. For $a > 0$ this is the uniform probability distribution with density $1/(2a)$ on the interval; for $a \le 0$ the set…
nodes.title: Uniform distribution on a symmetric interval

nodes.summary: A point $x$ of the one-dimensional Euclidean space lies in the unit interval body if and only if its single coordinate $x_1$ satisfies $-1/2 \le x_1 \le 1/2$.
nodes.title: Membership in the unit interval body

nodes.summary: The unit interval body is the closed interval $[-1/2, 1/2]$, of length one and centred at the origin, in the one-dimensional Euclidean space, regarded as a full-dimensional convex body.
nodes.title: Unit interval body
Probability

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
